record.file_problem: Repo metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a harmful-minus-harmless difference-of-means direction used in weight orthogonalization, and measures the resulting refusal rate. This tests the removal effect using a practical weight edit, rather than the original activation-ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The refusal-rate comparison is claim-bearing. The AI-disclaimer experiments concern a different behavior, not refusal or harmfulness judgments. Details such as separation scores and layer choices are not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal rates on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct before and after a weight-orthogonalization edit. The edit uses a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, applied to 10 top layers. That bears on whether the direction's removal eliminates refusal (V1), and on whether a weight edit removes it in a released model (V2). The method differs from the original: HF transformers, a partial-layer weight edit, and no activation addition.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author reports an 82% refusal reduction (100% to 18%) and treats refusal abliteration as successful. Citing Arditi et al., the author describes refusal as a single direction that can be cleanly removed, contrasting it with AI disclaimers, where abliteration removed the phrase but not the hedging style. The author does not acknowledge the 18% residual refusal as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the conventional harmful-minus-harmless mean difference, but performs weight orthogonalization rather than the original activation projection and uses HuggingFace transformers rather than TransformerLens. The README describes this as a learning project, not a replication.

fits_no_version.finding: A difference-in-means direction for 'As an AI...' disclaimers on leading questions, weight-ablated in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, cut disclaimers only 16.4% with 10 layers and 42.6% with all 28. The cautious hedging tone persisted after the phrase was removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means abliteration removes other assistant behaviors (e.g., AI self-identification disclaimers) less completely than refusal, and may remove only the surface marker.

record.problems: The README reports only 50 samples for the refusal comparison, provides no uncertainty estimate or null control, and does not report a general-capability evaluation. The code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing refusal results were left out. AI-disclaimer ablation results were omitted because they measure a different behavior, not refusal or harmfulness judgment.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; ablation at all layers and positions; preservation of other abilities (no capability evaluation); comparison with random-direction controls.
Capability cost of the edited checkpoint; models other than Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; results for the projected-abliteration variant, which is implemented but not reported.

missing.what: Layer count used for the refusal edit (10 top layers), plus separation score 9.8; needed as a condition on r1

record.verdict_notes: This is a personal learning project, not peer reviewed. There are 50 samples, no uncertainty estimate, no controls and no capability check. The code was not read, so the refusal-detection method and exact edit details are unverified. The example responses suggest compliance but are anecdotal.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction, activation ablation at every layer and position, or whether other abilities are largely preserved.
Only one released model is reported; generalization to other released models is untested.

tranche.reason: It uses a difference-in-means direction, but the weight orthogonalization covers only 10 layers rather than all of them. It is a HF-only reimplementation and the refusal scoring is not stated. That makes it a method variant on the same removal question, run on a model the original did not test. T3 is also arguable, but T2 is defensible.

source_check.notes: The text does not state the refusal scoring method (keyword or judge), whether the 50 test prompts are held out from the direction-extraction set, any capability measure, any control, or any uncertainty, and n=50 is a single run. '10 (top layers)' is the README's own wording and could mean the top-ranked layers (by separation score 9.8) rather than the final 10. The AI-disclaimer experiment (61/61 to 51/61 and 35/61) is not a refusal result and fits no version.
